newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico mine holds proven 47 million ounces silver.
newsitem.headline: Mexico mine holds proven 47 million ounces silver.

text.p: Mexico's Real del Monte mine in Pachuca state has proven reserves of 47 million silver ounces, the mine's part-owner Grupo Acerero del Norte (GAN) said in its bimonthly magazine.
The 456-year-old mine is owned by a joint venture between Denver-based Consolidated Nevada Goldfields Corp and GAN, the Mexican steel company said.

Real del Monte has produced 1.3 billion ounces of silver and 6.3 million ounces of gold. Consolidated Nevada president and CEO Geoffrey Hoyt has estimated silver output will rise to 2.7 million ounces in 1997, to 3.8 million ounces in 1998 and 5.3 million ounces in 1999.
GAN said Real del Monte has generated six percent of the world supply of silver over almost five centuries of production.
The joint venture has planned a five-year program to expand mineral extraction and search for further mines.
"Steps are being taken to be listed on the Mexico Stock Exchange," the magazine said.
GAN also said the companies' joint proven and probable reserves total 600,000 ounces of gold, 48 million ounces of silver, 28 million ounces of copper and four million metric tons of baryta.
